transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-04-05 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~32 minutes
Attendees: Maeve Carter (Redwood AE), Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Alpine CTO), Priya Shah (Lead ML Eng), Samir Patel (Infra)

Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect):
Maeve: quick intro, ask about current stack and what they want to try fast; Jordan: interested in quick POC, latency/cost, and data residency; Priya and Samir chime on infra constraints and SSO/SAML needs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maeve: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm maeve carter from redwood inference, i'll kick us off, we got diego from eng, you all?
[00:18] Jordan: yep, jordan here, thanks for making time, we've been kicking the tires on a few vendors, want to see how fast we can get something in prod via quickstart and what the tradeoffs are for hosted vs dedicated.
[00:30] Maeve: great, that is exactly what the quickstart is for - low time-to-first-token, free credits, sample prompts; diego do you want to jump in on what the self-serve path looks like?
[00:42] Diego: sure, so you can sign up, get free credits, create an api key, and call text-generation or embeddings via rest or our sdk. typical time to first token is under 5 minutes for a basic curl, like super fast, assuming no corporate network blocks. sometimes onboarding hits SSO if you're restricted.
[01:10] Priya: earlier you mentioned dedicated capacity - is that something you provision after the trial? and what are the latency improvements vs hosted?
[01:25] Maeve: yes, dedicated is reserved gpu pools, predictable throughput; hosted is multi-tenant. latency vs cost: dedicated gives more predictable p99 and lower tail latency, but you commit to reserved capacity and it's higher base cost.
[01:46] Samir: on data side, we need VPC peering and customer-managed KMS for keys - is private deployment required for that?
[01:55] Diego: private supports VPC and customer KMS, and on-prem can be an option if you need air-gapped. for most customers wanting KMS + VPC we do our private control plane model which keeps the operational overhead low. there can be some perf differences depending on where your traffic comes from.
[02:20] Jordan: our priority is to run a small pilot to validate latency and cost. would it make sense to start with hosted quickstart and then move to dedicated for pilot if we see noisy neighbors?
[02:35] Maeve: that's the typical flow - start self-serve, use credits, then if throughput needs increase we can propose a dedicated plan. quick note: we have automatic fallbacks and routing policies so if a region is out it can route to other variants, but that affects latency.
[02:58] Priya: how do you instrument costs? we need token-level breakdowns to attribute to product features.
[03:10] Diego: console gives token level cost and latency breakdowns per route and model, you can hook tracing and get per-request metrics. we also do recommendations on batching and quant profiles to reduce unit cost.
[03:34] Jordan: security checklist - SOC 2, SAML, audit logs, retention controls - is that all available for self-serve?
[03:46] Maeve: SOC 2 is available company-wide; for enterprise features like SAML SSO and custom retention you typically need a paid plan or dedicated/private. we'll send the security pack with the SOC 2 report and integration guide.
[04:05] Samir: any gotchas with firewall rules? egress to your hosted endpoints might be blocked by our corp policy.
[04:15] Diego: yep, we sometimes see corporate firewalls block outbound to hosted api endpoints; workaround is VPC peering or you can run a small proxy inside your network. for quickstart, you might need to allow api.redwood.ai ranges.
[04:35] Jordan: ok - what about model catalog? can we select quantized models to save cost?
[04:43] Maeve: yes, we surface model variants and quantization recommendations. you can choose smaller quant profiles for cheaper cost; SEs can recommend based on your prompt length distribution.
[04:58] Priya: on benching - diego, can you run a micro-benchmark? our typical request is 3 qps with ~128 tokens output per request.
[05:07] Diego: absolutely, if you share a sample prompt set and we get a trial account we can run the same workload against hosted and a dedicated config to compare p50/p95 and cost per 1k tokens.
[05:25] Jordan: what's the free credits typically for quickstart?
[05:30] Maeve: usually we issue $300-$500 in credits for evaluation, enough for small benchmarks - i'll confirm exact amount in the email.
[05:40] Samir: licensing/compliance - do you integrate with our cloud KMS?
[05:45] Diego: yes, we integrate with AWS KMS and GCP KMS; for HSM we have options on Private deployments.
[05:55] Priya: any hard limits on throughput or concurrency during trial?
[06:00] Maeve: self-serve accounts have soft quotas to protect the platform; we can bump for a trial POC on request. for heavy concurrency you'd want dedicated.
[06:15] Jordan: curious about the runtime - are you doing KV cache and prefix caching? basically can we get better perf for chat-like workloads?
[06:27] Diego: we do prefix and KV cache management, continuous batching; for chat workloads we manage the KV cache to reduce repeated computation. that tends to lower cost and latency together. sometimes transcriptions call KV as "kayvee" cache, sorry francophone issues.
[06:47] Maeve: (laughs) noted.
[06:50] Jordan: competitor question - we saw numbers from openai and anthropic, how do you differentiate?
[06:58] Maeve: mainly on production tooling, cost controls, and deployment flexibility; openai is great for ease, but if you need dedicated capacity and control over economics, redwood is opinionated there. we also emphasize observability and rollback/rollout features.
[07:18] Priya: any SDK samples we can try right now?
[07:22] Diego: yes, i'll drop a quick example in the doc. curl: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","prompt":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate - that will return streaming tokens if you want.
[07:40] Samir: streaming is supported? we want to do token-level streaming for UX.
[07:44] Diego: yep streaming & function calling are first class.
[07:48] Jordan: what about retention of logs and request audit trails?
[07:52] Maeve: we have audit logs, retention controls, and per-request tracing in the console. for strict retention policies enterprise plans provide longer retention and export.
[08:05] Priya: do you support SSO via SAML or OIDC?
[08:09] Maeve: yes SAML and OIDC - for self-serve you can do OIDC in many cases, SAML often needs a support-assisted setup for enterprise tenants.
[08:22] Jordan: great. timeline - we'd like a pilot next week if possible. is that feasible?
[08:28] Maeve: feasible if we get the quickstart account and sample prompts today; diego can run the micro-bench later this week. we'll set up a follow-up to review results.
[08:40] Samir: ok, one last infra detail: data residency, we have customers in eu and need eu-hosted endpoints. region support?
[08:50] Diego: we have regional endpoints in us and eu; private deployments can give you on-prem control if you need strict residency.
[09:02] Jordan: any price ballpark for dedicated? rough monthly commit for small pilot?
[09:08] Maeve: small dedicated starts in the low tens of thousands per month for a modest GPU pool; i'll include tiers in the pricing doc.
[09:20] Priya: will the micro-benchmark include cost estimates?
[09:24] Diego: yes i'll produce a spreadsheet with p50/p95 latency and approximate cost per 1k tokens, and show the impact of batching and quantization changes.
[09:36] Maeve: perfect. quick reshare of next steps: i'll send pricing, quickstart link, and security pack; diego will run bench once we have sample prompts and trial api key; jordan will create the trial account and share QPS and residency notes.
[09:53] Jordan: sounds good. any blockers from your side?
[09:57] Maeve: none, aside from needing the account info and prompts.
[10:02] Priya: thanks everyone.
[10:04] Maeve: thanks all - we'll follow up with the materials.
[10:08] (audio drops and minor crosstalk around 10:20-10:30 - auto-transcription may be noisy)
[10:30] Diego: i'll also include a sample notebook for local prototyping against the api.
[10:35] Jordan: appreciated.
[11:00] End of call.
